opposite_face_model.faces: the plus and minus Weyl characteristics are oppositely oriented local faces of one determinant-line descent object
opposite_face_model.local_sections: Delta_+ on U_+ and Delta_- on U_-

opposite_face_model.interpretation: the fifth/opposite tetrahedral face is not another scalar layer; it is the reciprocal Weyl chart needed to complete descent

unit_ambiguity.before_common_line: reciprocity and source grading alone permit many nowhere-zero symmetric factors exp(h(s)) with h(s)=h(1-s)

unit_ambiguity.lesson: a scalar ratio cannot establish the line identification; line identification must precede use of analytic continuation

kernel_gluing.required: Poisson maps gamma_+ and gamma_- and their cofactor/root-chain sections must transform by the same g_+- and reciprocal boundary operator
kernel_gluing.not_enough: gluing determinants while left/right kernel tensors use unrelated transitions
kernel_gluing.higher_cell: the mate cell is a determinant-and-kernel descent equivalence, not merely a functional equation for scalar values

Determine the transition law the adjugate must obey under C_+=L C_- R with invertible source-derived boundary frame changes, and isolate the anomaly if determinant and kernel transitions disagree.
iteration_result: The proposed opposite-face intuition is analytically correct in a precise sense: the second face is the reciprocal Weyl chart. A single Weyl function cannot become entire Xi, but the two oppositely oriented determinant charts can descend to one line section. The scalar phase completion happens only after this quotient/gluing, while kernel cofactors must descend in parallel.
